He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]]. ==Early life and high school career== Shead began his high school career at [[John B. Connally High School]] before transferring to Manor High School.{{cite news |last1=Baldwin |first1=Chris |title=Manor Mal — Houston’s Jamal Shead Is An Athletic Marvel Hiding In Plain Sight, But His Peyton Manning Level Leadership Leaps Out |url=https://www.papercitymag.com/culture/jamal-shead-houston-manor-mal-peyton-manning-leader-uh/ |access-date=February 10, 2024 |work=Paper City Magazine |date=February 8, 2023}} He averaged 18.1 points, six rebounds, and 3.9 assists per game as a junior. Shead led Manor High School to the state tournament for the first time in school history and scored 44 points in a win over [[Rudder High School]], earning District 18-5A Most Valuable Player honors.{{cite web |title=Houston Welcomes Three on Signing Day |url=https://uhcougars.com/news/2019/11/13/houston-mens-basketball-welcomes-three-on-national-signing-day |website=[[Houston Cougars]] |access-date=February 10, 2024 |date=November 13, 2019}} As a senior, he averaged 19.3 points and 4.3 assists per game, helping Manor achieve a 28–10 record and the District 18-5A title.{{cite news |last1=Jones |first1=Thomas |title=History already made, Manor seeks elusive state title |url=https://www.statesman.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/06/history-already-made-manor-seeks-elusive-state-basketball-title/53189043007/ |access-date=February 10, 2024 |work=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |date=March 6, 2019}} Considered a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by the [[247Sports]] Composite, Shead committed to playing college basketball for [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]] over [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]] and [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]].{{cite news |last1=Quinn |first1=Brendan |title=Jamal Shead was always a Houston player. Now the Coogs are his team |url=https://theathletic.com/4329774/2023/03/23/jamal-shead-houston-coogs-ncaa-tournament/ |access-date=February 10, 2024 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=March 23, 2023}} ==College career== As a freshman, Shead averaged 3.3 points and 1.5 assists per game, logging minor minutes as a backup point guard on [[2020–21 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston's 2020–21 Final Four team]].{{cite news |last1=Duarte |first1=Joseph |title=Houston’s Jamal Shead is on point when it comes to pressure and Sweet 16 |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/Houston-s-Jamal-Shead-is-on-point-when-it-comes-17024076.php |access-date=February 10, 2024 |work=[[Houston Chronicle]] |date=March 23, 2022}} In [[2021–22 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|2021–22]], Shead's sophomore season, he averaged 10 points and 5.8 assists per game. During the season he was promoted to the starting lineup after injuries to starting guards [[Marcus Sasser]] and Tramon Mark. Shead paced the Houston offense as the Cougars won both the AAC [[2021–22 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|regular season]] and [[2022 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|tournament]] championships. In the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], Shead averaged 15 points per game en route to an Elite Eight berth for the Cougars, which included an upset of South Regional No. 1 seed [[2021–22 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] in the Sweet 16, in which Shead led his team with 21 points.{{cite web |last1=Freeman |first1=Tristan |title=NCAA Basketball: Ranking the top 25 team backcourts for 2022-23 season |url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2022/07/18/ncaa-basketball-ranking-top-25-team-backcourts-2022-23-season/26/ |website=Busting Brackets |access-date=February 10, 2024 |date=July 18, 2022}} Shead was named to the All-[[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) Third Team.{{Cite web|url=http://theamerican.org/news/2022/3/8/american-athletic-conference-announces-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|title=American Athletic Conference Announces Men’s Basketball Honors|website=theamerican.org|language=en|date=March 8, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2024}} As a junior, he averaged 10.5 points, 5.4 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.7 steals per game. Shead was named to the All-AAC Second Team and earned AAC Defensive Player of the Year honors. Following the season, he declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]] but ultimately returned to Houston for his senior season.{{cite news |last1=Harris |first1=Terrance |title=UH guard Jamal Shead withdraws NBA Draft |url=https://defendernetwork.com/sports/professional/uh-guard-jamal-shead-withdraws-nba-draft/ |access-date=February 10, 2024 |work=The Houston Defender |date=June 3, 2023}} In [[2023–24 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|2023–24]], their first year in the [[Big 12 Conference men's basketball|Big 12]], Shead led the Cougars to a [[2023–24 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|regular season]] title with averages of 12.9 points, 6.3 assists, and 2.2 steals per game. He was named the [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] and Defensive Player of the Year, becoming the first player to win both awards in the same season.
